newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul won ends down despite central bank dlr sales.
newsitem.headline: Seoul won ends down despite central bank dlr sales.

text.p: The won closed lower against the U.S. unit on Monday on strong dollar buying for importer settlements which outweighed central Bank of Korea's dollar sales intervention, dealers said.
They said the central bank sold dollars twice in the morning session, once at 863.00 won and again at 865.00.
The won ended trading at 864.90, after opening the day at an intraday high of 857.70. It touched an intraday low of 865.10.
"The central bank's action slowed the dollar's rise, but the overall sentiment toward the greenback remained strong," said a domestic bank dealer.
Dealers said the central bank was expected to step in again at any time if the won's fall deepened, but predicted the U.S. unit will remain firm for the time being.

"Banks are unwilling to have long dollar positions for fear of losses from a sudden fall in the currency from central bank intervention. So importer deals are directly leading to a rise of the dollar," said a foreign bank dealer.
Dealers pegged the won's base mid-rate at 864.40 on Tuesday, compared to Monday's 856.70.
